title: A call and a direction
hook: The adhan you hear five times a day began as a dream. The direction you pray changed in the middle of a prayer.

screens.text: **The call to prayer you hear today began as a dream.** And the direction you face when you pray changed one afternoon, while people were in the middle of a prayer.

**How do we call people?** In the early years in Madinah, the Muslims talked about how to gather everyone for prayer. Then 'Abdullah ibn Zayd saw the words of the **adhan** (the call to prayer) in a dream [Abu Dawud 499; IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: The Prophet ﷺ said it was a true vision. 'Umar came running: he had seen the same thing [Abu Dawud 499].

screens.prompt: 'Abdullah ibn Zayd saw the dream. But he was told to teach the words to someone else to call out. Why?

options.text: Bilal had a louder, stronger voice
options.feedback: Right. The Prophet ﷺ chose Bilal for his voice, and 'Abdullah taught him the words [Abu Dawud 499].
Not quite. The reason given was simple: Bilal's voice carried further [Abu Dawud 499].

options.text: Only leaders could call the adhan
options.feedback: Not quite. Bilal wasn't a leader of any tribe. He was chosen for his voice.

screens.text: **The first voice.** You met Bilal in episode 12, refusing to give up "One, One" under torture [Ibn Majah 150]. He had been enslaved, and was freed, the early biographers say [Qalam ep. 37]. Now his voice called a whole city to prayer.
The worship you're learning takes shape.

events.title: The adhan
events.text: A dream, a true vision, and Bilal's voice [Abu Dawud 499].

events.title: Facing Jerusalem
events.text: In Madinah he prays toward Jerusalem, hoping for the Ka'bah [Bukhari 40].

events.title: The qibla turns
events.text: Allah turns the direction of prayer to the Ka'bah [Q 2:144].

events.title: Ramadan
events.text: Fasting Ramadan is made obligatory, the sources report [IslamQA 11575; Q 2:183].

screens.text: **Facing Jerusalem.** For sixteen or seventeen months in Madinah, he prayed toward Jerusalem. But he hoped to face the Ka'bah, the house Ibrahim built [Bukhari 40].
bubbles: Allah answered: *"We have certainly seen the turning of your face... toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased"* [Q 2:144, Saheeh Intl.].

options.feedback: Yes. The Sacred Masjid in Makkah, with the Ka'bah at its centre.
Not quite. They had faced al-Aqsa until then. This verse turned them to al-Masjid al-Haram.
Not quite. The verse turned them toward al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah.

screens.text: **Turning mid-prayer.** The first full prayer toward the Ka'bah was an 'Asr. A man who had prayed it passed another masjid where people were still praying toward Jerusalem. When he told them, they turned around right there, mid-prayer [Bukhari 40].
Turn the compass to face the Ka'bah, like those worshippers did mid-prayer. You learned this in Day 2.

**Real people, real history.** The adhan you hear, the direction you face, the month you fast: each has a story and real people behind it. When you face the **qibla**, you're turning with them, and with a freed man named Bilal calling you in.

screens.situation: Jordan prays at home, but feels like he's just copying moves from a video. Prayer feels mechanical, and he wonders if it means anything.

options.text: Learn the stories behind what he's doing, and keep praying while he learns
options.feedback: Yes. Knowing the dream, the voice and the turning gives every movement a story. Keep going.

options.text: Stop praying until it feels meaningful
options.feedback: Not quite. Meaning grows by showing up. The Companions turned mid-prayer because they were already praying.

options.text: Decide the details don't matter and face any direction
options.feedback: Not quite. The direction was a gift the Prophet ﷺ hoped for. Facing the Ka'bah joins him to every Muslim.

chips: What do the words of the adhan mean?

screens.text: Listen to the adhan like it's new.
steps: Play or listen to one adhan today
Remember the dream, and Bilal's voice, behind it
Answer it by going to pray

screens.text: A dream, a freed man's voice, and a city turning mid-prayer. The worship you're learning was lived by real people first.
Next episode: about three hundred against a thousand, at a place called Badr.

options.feedback: Right. 'Abdullah ibn Zayd dreamt the words; Bilal, with his stronger voice, called them [Abu Dawud 499].
Not quite. 'Umar had seen the same dream, but Bilal called the adhan.

check.prompt: Which way did the Muslims in Madinah face before the qibla changed?

options.feedback: Right. For sixteen or seventeen months, until Allah turned them to the Ka'bah [Bukhari 40].
Not quite. They faced Jerusalem, then the Ka'bah in Makkah.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The Muslims discussed how to call people to prayer. 'Abdullah ibn Zayd saw the words of the adhan in a dream; the Prophet ﷺ called it a true vision and had him teach it to Bilal, who had the louder voice; 'Umar had seen the same [Abu Dawud 499, Hasan Sahih]. The year is debated (1 or 2 AH); IslamQA 11575 says the second year, so say "in the early years in Madinah".
- Bilal had been tortured for his faith in Makkah and kept saying "One, One" [Ibn Majah 150, Hasan Sahih]; he had been enslaved and Abu Bakr bought his freedom, according to the early biographers [Qalam ep. 37]. (scholar question Q40)
- In Madinah he prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, hoping for the Ka'bah [Bukhari 40; Q 2:144].
- Allah turned the qibla to the Ka'bah [Q 2:144]; the first full prayer toward it was 'Asr, and people in another masjid turned mid-prayer when told [Bukhari 40].
- The fast of Ramadan was made obligatory in the second year [IslamQA 11575; Q 2:183].

**Likely questions**
- *"What do the words of the adhan mean?"* Give a plain meaning (Allah is the Greatest; I testify there is no god but Allah; I testify Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; come to prayer; come to success). Day 11 covers the adhan.
- *"Why did the qibla change?"* Keep to the texts: he hoped for it and Allah turned him [Q 2:144]. Don't add polemics about other faiths.
- *"Was Bilal a slave?"* Say plainly that slavery existed everywhere then; Bilal had been enslaved, was freed, and became the first voice of the adhan. Don't claim slavery is acceptable today or that Islam abolished it in one stroke; detailed questions go to the imam. (scholar question Q40)
- *"Prayer feels mechanical."* Normal; learn meanings bit by bit, slow down one prayer a day, keep praying. Mentor and Days 8–30.

**Escalate:** detailed questions on slavery (Q40).

**Don't**
- Don't present the qibla change as a rejection of Jews or Christians.
- Don't give a single certain year for the adhan.
sourcesMd:
- Qur'an [2:144](https://quran.com/2/144) (the qibla turned to al-Masjid al-Haram), [2:183](https://quran.com/2/183) (fasting decreed).
- [Abu Dawud 499](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:499) (Hasan Sahih, al-Albani; Isnad Hasan, Zubair Ali Zai): 'Abdullah ibn Zayd's dream; Bilal's louder voice; 'Umar's dream.
- [Bukhari 40](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:40) (Sahih): sixteen or seventeen months toward Jerusalem; the first 'Asr toward the Ka'bah; turning mid-prayer.
- [Ibn Majah 150](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:150) (Hasan Sahih, al-Albani): Bilal under torture saying "One, One".
- [IslamQA 11575, *Who Is Muhammad?*](https://islamqa.info/en/answers/11575): in the second year the adhan, the qibla change and the Ramadan fast.
- Qalam Institute, *The Sīrah Podcast*, [ep. 37, The torture and suffering of the early Muslims in Makkah](https://www.qalaminstitute.org/2013/02/seerah-life-of-the-prophet-the-torture-suffering-of-the-early-muslims-in-makkah/): Bilal freed by Abu Bakr.
- Fact rows 24.1–24.5 and 12.1 in Seerah Fact-Check Log.
